body.heading: First, cool the room down
paragraphs: When siblings clash, the first job is rarely finding out who started it. It is lowering the temperature: separate the combatants kindly, hand out water, let voices come down. Investigations held at full volume produce only louder evidence.
You do not need a verdict to restore peace. Often the honest summary is 'you both wanted the same thing at the same time', which is true of most adult disagreements too.

body.heading: Each story, uninterrupted
paragraphs: When things are calm, each child tells their version without interruption, and the other listens — a skill that takes years to learn and starts here. Reflect back the feeling before the facts: 'you felt left out' lands before 'he had the crayon first'.
Resist appointing a villain. Ask each child what they wish had happened and what they could do next time. You are teaching a method, not just ending a noise.

body.heading: Repair is the ending that matters
paragraphs: An apology forced at speed means little; a small repair — returning the toy, rebuilding the knocked-down tower together, drawing a peace picture — means more. Let the repair be their idea where you can, and accept clumsy ones graciously.
And some days the kindest ruling is a change of scene: a snack, a walk, a different game. Not every squabble needs a summit meeting.

description: Cool things down first, hear each side without interruption, and end with a small repair rather than a forced apology.
